analysis_scope: application and DU Cell evidence collected from 2026-08-15 through 2026-08-18 for 70/20/10 and 40/40/20

prior_campaign_correction.scope: all application experiments collected before the August 15-16 TDD diagnostic
prior_campaign_correction.note: Earlier records that labeled these campaigns 40/40/20 are incorrect. Their application results remain valid, but they are all 70/20/10 observations and do not form a TDD comparison.

du_cell_alignment.timestamp_timezone_status: inferred from experiment-volume alignment; not vendor-confirmed
du_cell_alignment.primary_bin_rule: complete nonzero-duration five-minute bins fully contained in one run window, matched to the serving cell, with nonzero unavailability bins excluded or flagged
du_cell_alignment.throughput_rule: recompute 1000 * sum(volume_kb) / sum(active_time_ms); do not average exported throughput rows
du_cell_alignment.metric_boundary: cell-level volume and active-time context; not endpoint goodput, radio capacity, per-request latency, or a per-UE measurement

uplink_heavy_latency_result.scope: vehicle-to-d1 IPI workload request plus compact correlated acknowledgment RTT
uplink_heavy_latency_result.reason: No timestamp-aligned, same-cell DU pair exists across the two TDD profiles. The August 15 40/40/20 raw run and timestamps are absent, and the August 16 70/20/10 run occurs after the retained DU data end. The 40/40/20 repetitions also changed serving cell and cell state.
uplink_heavy_latency_result.conclusion: The uplink-heavy observations cannot establish whether 40/40/20 or 70/20/10 provides lower application RTT.

du_context.du_coverage: none; experiment starts at 15:55:49 EDT and retained DU rows end at 15:15 EDT

valid_uses: report each run as an observation of its recorded operating state
report the close same-profile 70/20/10 repeat values
use the DU export to confirm the serving traffic cell and cell-unavailability context
prohibited_inferences: rank 40/40/20 and 70/20/10 by uplink-heavy application RTT
attribute the August 15-16 uplink-heavy RTT differences to TDD allocation alone
pool the August 17 or August 18 direction and signal conditions into the August 15-16 uplink result

downlink_heavy_latency_result.scope: compact vehicle request plus exact 1, 10, 100, or 500 KiB d1-to-vehicle response at location 3 on 2026-08-17
downlink_heavy_latency_result.application_conclusion: 40/40/20 lowers p50 and p95 RTT for 1-10 KiB responses, but its advantage disappears at 500 KiB TCP and reverses in the p95 tail for 100-500 KiB MQTT.
downlink_heavy_latency_result.du_interpretation: Both selected windows are strongly downlink-heavy and contain no reported cell unavailability. The DU counters confirm the cell-level traffic context but do not identify the mechanism behind the application RTT differences.

exact_50mib_goodput_result.scope: ten sequential exact 52,428,800-byte TCP uploads and ten exact downloads per TDD profile at location 3 on 2026-08-17

upload_vehicle_to_d1.comparison: 40/40/20 measured application goodput is 76.4 percent lower; 70/20/10 is 4.23 times higher

download_d1_to_vehicle.comparison: 40/40/20 measured application goodput is 21.3 percent lower; 70/20/10 is 1.27 times higher

exact_50mib_goodput_result.du_boundary: The bulk experiment alternates upload and download inside the same five-minute DU bins. DU counters are not used to estimate direction-specific endpoint goodput.

weak_signal_direction_result.scope: 2026-08-18 MQTT 500 KiB at 40/40/20, location 3, serving Cell 2, and -115 dBm
weak_signal_direction_result.conclusion: Application direction dominates communication latency for the matched large-object weak-signal condition.

profile_40_40_20.artifact_status: coauthor-reported; raw trace not present in the current repository
